item.title: Advanced Patterns
item.description:
This advanced workshop explores architectural patterns, performance optimization, and enterprise practices for building scalable, maintainable OutSystems applications.

What You’ll Learn

  • Scalability patterns and architecture
  • Security best practices
  • Performance optimization techniques
  • Team collaboration patterns
  • Testing strategies at scale

Architectural Patterns

Layered Architecture

Separating concerns into distinct layers improves maintainability and scalability.

Event-Driven Architecture

Decoupling services through events enables better scalability and resilience.

Performance Optimization

  • Database query optimization
  • Caching strategies
  • Asynchronous processing
  • Load balancing

Conclusion

Enterprise architecture requires careful planning and deep understanding of patterns and best practices.

item.title: Getting Started
item.description:
Welcome to the OutSystems Developer Workshops! This series is designed to take you from beginner to advanced developer on the OutSystems low-code platform.

What You’ll Learn

This workshop series covers:

  1. Behavior-Driven Development (BDD) — Learn how to write specifications that guide development
  2. OutSystems Basics — Master the fundamentals of the OutSystems platform
  3. Advanced Patterns — Explore enterprise-scale architecture and best practices

Workshop Structure

Each module is self-contained yet builds on previous knowledge. You can follow them sequentially or jump to specific topics based on your experience level.

item.title: OutSystems Basics
item.description:
OutSystems is a leading low-code platform for rapid application development. This workshop covers the fundamentals of building applications on the OutSystems platform.

What You’ll Learn

  • Navigate the OutSystems Studio IDE
  • Create your first application
  • Work with data and databases
  • Build responsive user interfaces
  • Understand the application architecture

Platform Introduction

OutSystems enables developers to build enterprise applications faster with less code.

Key Concepts

  • Modules — Self-contained code units
  • Entities — Data models and database tables
  • Screens — User interface components
  • Actions — Logic and business processes
